full_judgment:
This rule is directed against the Judgment and decree dated 5-6-2004 Passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla, in Title Appeal No. 210 of 2001 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 5-7-2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chauddagram, Comilla, in Title Suit No. 44 of 1994 decreeing the suit. 

 2. Facts, in short, are that a suit for partition being No. 44 of 1994 was decreed ascertaining the plaintiffs share to the extent of 1.05½ acres. The defendant Nos. 1-7 and 53 also got a saham to the extent of 36 decimals. That preliminary decree was not challenged in appeal. 

 3. The plaintiff submitted an application for making the decree final and accordingly a Commissioner was appointed. The learned Advocate Commissioner serving due notice upon the parties executed a commission and submitted a report making final allotment of saham. The report was objected by the defendants, contending inter alit?, that one of the huts of the defendant was allotted to the saham of the plaintiffs share and the pathway used by the defendants was allotted to the saham of the plaintiff making a great inconvenience to them. The learned Advocate Commissioner was examined in Court and was cross-examined. The learned Assistant Judge after considering the evidence on record accepted the Commissioner's report, rejected the objection and made the decree final by the Judgment and decree dated 8-7-2001 against which the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 210 of 2001. The Court of appeal dismissed the appeal and affirmed the final decree by the impugned judgment and decree against which the instant Rule. 

 4. Mr Subhas Chandra Saha, the learned Advocate for the petitioner appearing for the petitioner took me through the commissioner report, objection submitted against the Commission report and the evidence on record. He submitted that as per own admission of the Advocate Commissioner a part of the defendant's homestead was allotted to the saham of the plaintiff and as such the final decree is liable to be set aside and a fresh commission required to be made for effecting equitable partition. He further submitted that the pathway of the defendant for going to the pond has been allotted to the saham of the plaintiff by which the defendants are facing very much inconvenience. 

 7. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates. I have perused the commission report, objection filed by the defendant against the report, the evidence on record and the impugned judgment and decree. 

 9. It is not unusual that at the time of Final Partition some of the possessor would be affected and some of the decree holder would be benefited. 

 11. In view of the above although the submissions as made by Mr Saha appears to be meaningful but since the defendants were allotted saham maintaining 36 decimals of land, it would not be justified to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. Since the defendant's have not been allotted share Sesser than that of their actual saham, I do not find any cogent ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. 

 12. In view of the above I find no merit in the Rule. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 5-6-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla, in Title Appeal No. 210 of 2001 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 5-7-2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chauddagram, Comilla, in Title Suit No. 44 of 1994 decreeing the suit is hereby affirmed. The order of stay dated 11-12-2004 granted by this Court stands vacated.
